title: Gödel's Theorem follows from the universality of arithmetic, shown via rule 110

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gödel's Theorem follows from the universality of arithmetic, shown via rule 110

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: An integer (exponential Diophantine) equation can be built whose solutions emulate the rule 110 cellular automaton; since rule 110 is universal, the axioms of arithmetic support universality, which implies Gödel's Theorem that arithmetic contains statements that cannot be proved true or false. Wolfram presents Gödel's Theorem as a consequence of the Principle of Computational Equivalence.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And with the cellular automaton being a universal one such as rule 110 this implies that the axioms of arithmetic can support universality.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Implications for Mathematics and Its Foundations” (from p. 772), p. 785. Scope: axioms of integer arithmetic (Peano arithmetic) and Diophantine encodings of cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-34: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Every component is a finite mathematical construction or theorem that can be checked against public proofs. The philosophical attribution to the Principle of Computational Equivalence is not needed to test the formal implication.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Check an explicit Diophantine encoding of rule 110 evolution, the proof of rule 110 universality, and the logical reduction from effective arithmetic expressiveness to incompleteness under the required consistency assumptions. A failed encoding or invalid implication refutes this proposed derivation, while a verified chain confirms it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Universality alone must be linked carefully to representability and provability.

Gödel incompleteness requires consistency and effective axiomatizability assumptions.

An exponential Diophantine equation is not automatically an ordinary polynomial equation.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both ingredients are published and checkable: rule 110 is universal by Cook's proof, and incompleteness of arithmetic is a formalized theorem. The distinctive step is the integer equation that emulates rule 110, which is explicit and is a finite certificate a proof-oriented check can accept or reject. The claim is this implication, and the resources to check it exist.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Verify that solutions of the stated exponential Diophantine equation encode rule 110 histories, using the published proof that rule 110 is universal, and apply the standard translation from an undecidable cellular-automaton question to a statement independent of arithmetic. A break in the encoding refutes this derivation; a checked encoding confirms it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The displayed exponential Diophantine equation is large, so checking every clause is specialist work.

Other proofs of incompleteness exist, so a gap in this encoding would refute the route rather than incompleteness itself.
